summary.intent: Use /gsd:manager to discuss, plan, and execute the v1.1 hardening block (phases 51-55 of CipherBox), then complete the full ship loop for Phase 51 including verify, secure, validate, simplify, CodeRabbit CLI review, and PR creation with resolve-pr-reviews.
summary.outcome: All 5 hardening phases (51-55) were discussed and planned in parallel isolated git worktrees (21 plans total); Phase 51 was fully executed and shipped as PR #529 after catching a build-breaking compile error, an S3 zeroization regression causing 48/89 E2E failures, and two rounds of CodeRabbit hardening improvements. PR #529 is open with CI green but thread resolution was incomplete at session end.

repo: GSD executor's `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` gate never compiles the desktop Tauri crate — cross-crate type changes (e.g. unwrap_key returning Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>) silently break apps/desktop and are only caught by the verify step's full `cargo check --workspace`.

GSD commit style 'feat 51-03:' (type + plan-id + colon) is not conventional commits format and fails the required 'Release Preview' CI check on any PR touching versioned packages; 13 commits had to be bulk-reworded via `git filter-branch --msg-filter`.
git push is blocked by the Claude Code sandbox on port 443 even though `curl https://github.com` succeeds; requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` for push commands.
gsd-tools `query commit` helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative when the commit actually landed — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying.

Background GSD plan-phase agents CAN nest subagents on this harness (general-purpose/claude agents have Tools:*); the manager workflow's 'no nesting in background on Claude Code' guardrail is overly conservative.

The #683 auto-degrade fires automatically when a worktree's HEAD has diverged from origin/HEAD (shouldDegrade:true), forcing execute-phase to run sequentially in-tree — which is correct when the worktree already has pnpm deps installed.
pnpm i must be run in each worktree; node_modules symlinks conflict with pre-commit hooks (lint-staged) and pnpm's resolution logic.
SDK E2E is the only CI gate that exercises cross-package IPNS publish round-trips; unit suites (jest/vitest) mock parseIpnsRecord and miss integration regressions on the publish path.
CodeRabbit bundles findings in the review body (not inline threads) when findings are 'outside diff range'; /resolve-pr-reviews must parse the review body text, not just thread replies.

The init.manager dep parser misparses phase names containing parenthesized version strings (e.g. 'Phase 49 (v1.1 baseline)') as having a phantom '1.1' dependency, causing recommended_actions to return empty for unblocked phases.

The release-please stale-pin issue (#16) was caused by a force-pushed branch orphaning the bot's commit + cancel-in-progress killing the recompute; fix is fetch+rebase discipline, not pin-clearing machinery.

Phase 55 (lib.rs decomposition into 6 modules) must execute AFTER Phase 51+52 merge to main — both touch crates/fuse/src/lib.rs and rebasing a file-split over functional changes would create brutal merge conflicts.

code.finding: createAndPublishIpnsRecord must NOT zero params.ipnsPrivateKey in its finally block. The client caches per-folder IPNS keys in folderTree and publishWithCas reuses the same buffer across retries and mutations. Zeroing in this callee caused 48/89 SDK E2E failures (second publish derived pubkey from zeros → wrong ipnsName → 400). Contract is caller-owns-key; terminal owners (vault, shared-write, bin) each zero their own buffer.

publishWithCas passes the same params object (including ipnsPrivateKey buffer) to createAndPublishIpnsRecord on every CAS retry and across mutations. Any callee that zeroes params.ipnsPrivateKey will corrupt subsequent operations.

S2 empty-string edge case: `if (signatureV2 || data || pubKey)` treats empty-string fields as falsy, silently downgrading to legacy verification when all three are empty strings. Must use explicit nullish checks: `if (signatureV2 != null || data != null || pubKey != null)`.

root_folder_key field changed from RwLock<Option<Vec<u8>>> to RwLock<Option<zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>> (CodeRabbit finding #3). Desktop vault.rs now stores the Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> directly from unwrap_key() without .to_vec() downgrade.

S3 Zeroizing cascade: unwrap_key() return type change to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> broke this desktop consumer which stored into a plain Vec field. The executor's cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse gate never compiled this crate — only caught by the verify step's full workspace cargo check.

Pre-existing bug (Phase 23 #352, NOT Phase 51): on PublishResult::Conflict, the per-file IPNS sequence is still recorded as successfully published — data integrity bug in the FUSE-durability domain (Phase 52 scope). Phase 51 diff only reformatted the log::warn! on this branch.

The E2E 400s were NOT from the new S1 CID/sequence checks — they came from the pre-existing publicKey→ipnsName derivation check at line 77, triggered when the caller's key was zeroed. The S1 round-trip CID check is lossless for both CIDv0 and CIDv1.
Three identical IPNS field base64-decode-and-map-err blocks consolidated into a local closure (simplify step). api-client 6/6 tests green.

workflow: Parallel phase planning works reliably with per-phase git worktrees: `git worktree add <path> <branch>`, run `pnpm i` in the worktree, pass RUNTIME_DIR to the plan-phase skill. Three planners running in parallel (p51/p52/p53) with no lock collisions.

Full ship loop ordering: verify → secure → validate → simplify → CodeRabbit CLI (before ship) → ship → resolve-pr-reviews. Running CodeRabbit CLI before opening the PR allows fixing findings before the PR review starts.

S3 zeroization contract: callees that receive key buffers must NEVER zero them. Only terminal owners (the function that allocates and knows the key won't be reused) should zero. Document the contract: 'CALLER RETAINS OWNERSHIP'.

git filter-branch --msg-filter works for bulk non-interactive commit subject rewrites when rebase -i is unavailable. Pattern: `--msg-filter 'sed -E "1 s/^([a-z]+) [0-9][0-9A-Za-z.-]*: /\1: /"'` rewrites GSD-style to conventional; drops signatures but required_signatures:false makes this safe.

When a background agent is interrupted (session limit), check its worktree HEAD before re-launching — it may have already committed partial work. Inspect `git log` and uncommitted changes before deciding what to re-run.

cargo fmt churn: editing a previously unformatted file causes pre-commit hooks to reflow the entire file. Revert and apply only targeted minimal edits to avoid polluting the PR diff with 280-line whitespace changes.

Adversarial verify workflow: after applying a batch of fixes, spawn independent agents per fix domain instructed to find key leaks or incorrect logic. Confirmed all fixes ok:true before committing; caught pre-existing cas.test.ts tsc issue in the process.

friction: Two session-limit interruptions mid-work: first cut off the Phase 51 plan agent mid-start; second cut off the #1/#2 Zeroizing fixer mid-commit. Both required state inspection and careful resume.
Initial Phase 51 plan agent was launched without worktree isolation (shared main tree with 52's discussion), requiring user intervention to stop the agent and establish the worktree pattern.
GSD executor's cargo test gate doesn't compile the desktop Tauri crate — Zeroizing return-type cascade to vault.rs:210 wasn't caught until verify step.
GSD commit style is non-conventional, failing required Release Preview CI — 13 commits had to be bulk-reworded after the PR was already open.
git push blocked by sandbox on port 443 (curl works fine) — required dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true; wasn't discovered until late in the session during the fix-commit push.
gsd-tools commit helper false negative ('commit_failed') fired multiple times throughout the session, requiring redundant git log verification each time.

S3 zeroization regression (48/89 E2E failures) was only discovered after PR #529 was opened — required local API spin-up, client rebuild, and multiple instrumentation passes to diagnose the exact 400 message.
SDK E2E full reproduction required rebuilding 4 client packages before failures reproduced locally, adding significant diagnosis time.
CodeRabbit found an empty-string edge case in my own S2 fix only after the second push — `if (a || b || c)` treats '' as falsy — requiring a third commit round.
Background CI/CodeRabbit poll exited early on empty JSON (checks hadn't registered yet post-push) — needed manual re-query and re-arm.
